title: Your first part
intro: Describe a part in plain words. The agent writes build123d code, the exact kernel builds it, and the viewer updates. Then change a number by hand and watch it rebuild without the agent.

steps.text: Make a 60 × 40 × 8 mm mounting plate with four Ø5 holes 8 mm in from each corner, and a Ø20 boss 15 mm tall in the middle with a Ø8 through bore. Call it Plate.
steps.narr: The design is empty. You describe the part in plain words in the chat. Give the dimensions you care about; the agent will turn them into named parameters.

steps.text: I'll build that as one body with named dimensions so you can tweak them later.
steps.narr: The agent replies like a colleague: a one-line plan, then it gets to work.

steps.name: build_model
steps.code:
# Mounting plate with a bossed bore
plate_l, plate_w, plate_t = 60, 40, 8
boss_d, boss_h, bore_d = 20, 15, 8
hole_d, inset = 5, 8
with BuildPart() as plate:
    Box(plate_l, plate_w, plate_t)
    with Locations((0, 0, plate_t / 2)):
        Cylinder(boss_d / 2, boss_h, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))
    Hole(bore_d / 2)
    with Locations((-plate_l/2 + inset, -plate_w/2 + inset), (plate_l/2 - inset, -plate_w/2 + inset),
                   (-plate_l/2 + inset, plate_w/2 - inset), (plate_l/2 - inset, plate_w/2 - inset)):
        Hole(hole_d / 2)
result = {"Plate": plate.part}
steps.result: Model OK: 1 body, 13 faces, total volume=22128.0mm³
steps.narr: It calls the build_model tool with a build123d script (shown at the bottom left, and under 'code ▸' on the card). The result line is the kernel's verdict: bodies, faces and volume, or a traceback the agent then fixes.
The viewer shows the exact model as soon as the script builds. Drag to orbit. Every face is true B-rep geometry; the triangles you see are display only.

steps.text: Done — **Plate**: 60 × 40 × 8 plate, Ø20 × 15 boss with a Ø8 through bore, four Ø5 holes on a 44 × 24 pattern. Volume 22,128 mm³. The dimensions are parameters at the top of the script (plate_l, boss_d, hole_d…), so say the word to change any of them.
steps.narr: The agent confirms what it built with numbers that came back from the kernel, not from its own arithmetic.
Now without the agent: the Design tab lists every top-level number in the script as a field. Change boss_h from 15 to 20 and press Enter.
The part rebuilt with a 20 mm boss. Only that literal in the script changed, and the agent is sent a note about it so it stays in sync.

steps.text: Set the boss back to 15 tall, fillet the four vertical corner edges 4 mm, then export a STEP.
steps.narr: Back to chat. Parameter edits and requests mix freely because both end up in the same script.

steps.name: build_model
steps.code:
# Mounting plate with a bossed bore
plate_l, plate_w, plate_t = 60, 40, 8
boss_d, boss_h, bore_d = 20, 15, 8
hole_d, inset = 5, 8
with BuildPart() as plate:
    Box(plate_l, plate_w, plate_t)
    with Locations((0, 0, plate_t / 2)):
        Cylinder(boss_d / 2, boss_h, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))
    Hole(bore_d / 2)
    with Locations((-plate_l/2 + inset, -plate_w/2 + inset), (plate_l/2 - inset, -plate_w/2 + inset),
                   (-plate_l/2 + inset, plate_w/2 - inset), (plate_l/2 - inset, plate_w/2 - inset)):
        Hole(hole_d / 2)
    fillet(plate.edges().filter_by(Axis.Z).group_by(Axis.X)[0] + plate.edges().filter_by(Axis.Z).group_by(Axis.X)[-1], 4)
result = {"Plate": plate.part}
steps.result: Model OK: 1 body, 17 faces, total volume=22018.1mm³
steps.narr: The agent rewrites the script: boss_h back to 15 and a fillet on the four vertical corner edges, selected by axis rather than by guessing edge numbers.
Fillets are true cylindrical faces. STEP export writes them as cylindrical surfaces, never as triangles.

steps.name: export_model
steps.narr: export_model writes the STEP file into workspace/exports. STL is different: it is tessellated only at export, at a tolerance you choose.

steps.text: Boss back to 15 mm, the four vertical plate edges filleted at R4, and **plate.step** exported (exact geometry, one solid). The hole pattern is unchanged.
steps.narr: That is the whole loop: describe, build, check, adjust. Next: pointing at a face so the agent works on exactly the geometry you mean.
